title: The Toll That Grows Three Ways
story: At the Cloudstep Tollhouse, a spectacled badger named Wrathcombe charges pilgrims a fee that nobody can ever untangle. Today a family of pilgrims owes a base toll of 80 gold crowns, plus a 25% "sky-draft surcharge" on that base, minus a 10% "walked-in-mud discount" taken off the new total. Mr 6 pulls out his scratch slate.
question: How many gold crowns should the family actually pay?
solution: The surcharge is 25% of 80 = 20 crowns, so the total becomes 80 + 20 = 100 crowns.
The discount is 10% of 100 = 10 crowns, so 100 - 10 = 90 crowns.
praise: Adding the surcharge first was exactly right — the discount then had to come off the NEW total, not the old one.
hint: Do it in order: find the surcharge on 80 first, then take 10% off whatever that new total is.
victory: Wrathcombe checked the slate twice, snorted, and stamped the ledger APPROVED. Mr 6 now gets free passage forever — the badger says honest arithmetic is rarer than gold.
imagePrompt: A stout spectacled badger in a clerk's visor behind a tall tollhouse desk on a cliffside cloud bridge, a numeral-six knight holding up a chalk slate of neat calculations while pilgrims watch hopefully in misty morning light.
